title: Structured Output — JSON Schema, Pydantic, Zod, Constrained Decoding
service: InvoiceKit: invoice extraction from model replies, with a JSON Schema subset validator, typed outcomes, a JSON result snapshot, a retry loop, a constrained decoder and discriminated oneOf

parts.lesson_anchor: code/main.py validate and process_model_output; The three failure modes; Pydantic: ValidationError with typed error paths; JSON Schema 2020-12 enum
planted_bugs: _at stores array indices in loc as str, so paths print as $.line_items.0.sku; the TypeError surfaces two calls later, in lookup called by feedback
the array branch returns at the first element with errors, so the errors of later line items are lost
process_model_output parses before checking the __REFUSAL__ prefix, so the refusal branch is dead code and a refusal becomes a parse_error
enum is a linear scan with _same_json, O(lines x SKUs)
parts.timing_assert: 3,000 line items against a 5,000-SKU enum under 0.1 s (the linear scan takes 1.09-1.14 s on this machine under light load and 3-5 s under heavy load; the indexed version 4.5-4.9 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: enum keeps JSON equality: false is not 0 and true is not 1, 5.0 equals 5, objects compare member by member in any key order and are unhashable, so set(enum), the lesson's list membership, repr keys and json.dumps keys all fail; and validate must not cache its index inside the schema

parts.lesson_anchor: Pydantic: total_usd: Decimal; Refusals: a first-class outcome; the three failure modes kept with the raw reply
parts.storage: one JSON snapshot file, rewritten through a temporary file in the same directory and os.replace; Decimal saved as a tagged string with all its digits; a payload object shaped like a tag, such as a model-written {"$decimal": "1"}, is saved as {"$object": [[key, value]]}
parts.exactness: ok, violation, parse_error and refusal results round-trip across reopen: Decimal('120.00') keeps its digits (checked with exact(), since Decimal('120.0') == Decimal('120.00')), model-quoted strings like "49.99" stay strings, error locations come back as tuples with int indices, raw replies and refusal reasons keep every character

deviations: Part 1: error paths are typed locations (a loc tuple of str and int, rendered as $.line_items[0].sku), after the Pydantic section's 'typed error paths'. The path bug therefore surfaces in feedback/lookup, two calls from the root cause, instead of as a wrong string. The enum check in the starter already has JSON-equality semantics and is only slow, so the set over-fix is a real guard; validate must also leave the schema unchanged.

Part 2: Decimal amounts are saved as tagged strings ({"$decimal": "120.00"}) rather than read back with parse_float=Decimal, because violation payloads hold model-quoted strings such as "49.99" that must stay strings. parse_float=Decimal is used when replies are parsed (process_model_output), and JSON numbers read back with parse_float=Decimal are also accepted. The snapshot also holds a totals violation from Part 3, so rebuilding results from the raw reply is caught.
Part 3: feedback() from Part 1 is the injected note, and it carries every error path; the business rule also has to accept 220 for 220.00 and sub-cent prices without rounding.

Part 4: besides objects with fixed property order, string enums and non-negative integers, a bare integer schema is decoded to exercise EOS and leading zeros; the stand-in model is keyed by the text so far, with detours that make wrong decoders produce visibly wrong output.
Part 5: bundles add one nested level of discriminated oneOf, and a separate discount oneOf without a discriminator tests exactly-one matching on the integer/number overlap.
